findings.reason: the plan's own plan-after is kernel-compile-barrier, whose §0 sets explicit bounds (compile wall at most 60 s on the H200 with the warm cache excluded, executable at most 50 MB, at most 64 GB resident during a cold compile), so s3's 13568-square build at half cell size would be accepted at any cost the node happens to measure and the census row it writes carries no verdict.
findings.text: s3 done-when (2) requires only that "the compile time and the warm execute time each recorded at 1696 cells and on the prototype mesh at half its cell size", and done-when (3) that the program "appears in the kernel-compile census", so neither clause can fail on cost: the only falsifiable part of (2) is the cache hit, and every scale and duration passes

findings.reason: a node held to a threshold that omits the cell-sum term either fails a correct device build or is forced to widen the tolerance after the fact; §2 also records the term per slope (line 215, "the best attainable error and the ε that gives it recorded per slope") while the 1696-cell mesh mixes slopes, so the clause names no single number a worker can apply.
findings.text: the tolerance is "the rounding term of §2's measured error curve at the production strip width", described as "the cancellation between a strip's two long edges inside one Part V evaluation", and the clause then asserts "the order in which a cell's edge sheets are added does not touch it"; but G's columns are signed sums of a cell's four edge sheets, which near-cancel at a distant target (that is why a uniformly magnetised cell's far field is a dipole and why a shared edge appears once with the net sheet (M1 − M2)×n), so the sum carries a cancellation amplification the single-strip term does not contain, and it is header-blind to whether device and host add in the same order

findings.reason: the clause's stated purpose is "so a production mesh's cost is read from the census rather than re-measured", and with no polygon-tile row a worker must invent the measurement shape and the census stops being the single ledger it is cited as.
findings.text: done-when (3) requires the program to be "measured the same way as the polygon tile", but docs/research/compile-cost-evidence.html carries no polygon-tile measurement: its program rows are harmonic_multiply, harmonic_moments, harmonic_pole_moments, packed_analytic_moments, point_jet, production_point_batch, prototype_point_batch, topology_read and certificate_map, and the strings tile_evaluator, tile_coupling and _fill_tile appear nowhere in the document

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — "measured the same way as the polygon tile" cites a census row that does not exist in docs/research/compile-cost-evidence.html, which carries no tile_evaluator, tile_coupling or _fill_tile program.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — s3 done-when (2) and (3) only require the compile wall and memory to be recorded, so a build that takes an hour and 100 GB passes them unchanged.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — done-when (3) lands the row in the in-repo census document docs/research/compile-cost-evidence.html, and the heavy gates run on betelgeuse under gpu_0003_grpA as one job; no session or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — s3 introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags; §2 and §3 are cross-references to plan sections, not symbols a later reader needs a tracker to resolve.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the device-versus-host tolerance is set to a single strip's rounding term while G is a signed sum of four edge sheets per cell, and the sentence asserting that the addition order does not touch the tolerance is unsupported.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, the device build of G through the existing tile plan; the three clauses measure its accuracy, its cost and its cache behaviour.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s3 declares depends-on iron-core-magnetisation#s2, which is where the sheet route and the strip width it consumes are decided, and s4 and s6 both declare s3; the mesh it measures on is the §1 prototype mesh, and §1 is done.
